title: Housing Issues
paragraphs: “Um, are you probably referring to Lord Elmero? From what I’ve heard, it all started with a message from the Spear Hero, and the Shield Hero came to the Puhant family estate to investigate.”
“That’s right.”
“Whoa… So this is the Spear Hero? Is this really okay? Seriously?”
“Is this it?” That’s quite a thing to say. To tell you the truth, I am The Love Hunter!
“His strength is the stuff of legend. Not to mention the fact that he’s the one who cornered that Takt gang, on top of the folks from Shieldfreeden.”

The servants, Beastmen, and slaves are all buzzing with excitement. I knew it, I knew it. I’ve taken down both Shieldfreeden and Takt with this spear. You should take a good look at it. It’s a sacred spear blessed by Filo-tan and Filolial-sama, after all.
“So, Spear Hero, what would you like to know?　Is it about Lord Elmero? Or perhaps the Puhant family’s schemes?”
“I’d like to know pretty much everything there is to know. Though, if possible, it would probably be faster to just bring Father here…”
“That would be an honor… but I doubt the Puhant family would ever allow such a thing…”

Well, they’re the sort of people who hide their servants and slaves even during inspections. They’re probably keeping track of Father’s whereabouts at all times. That’s exactly why I’m gathering information myself.
“I could teleport you two—since you know the situation—to the castle… but before that, it seems Father and the others are planning a banquet and various other events…”

I imagine Father and his party will remain at the Zou residence at least until nightfall. It’ll be tricky to find a plausible excuse to cut the inspection short. Well, since the Zou family seems to be underestimating Father, he’ll likely try to slip away once they slip up and use that as his excuse.
But… this all started out of my own goodwill toward Zou, who raised Kou so well. I’ll do my best to listen as much as I can. I’ll do my best to bring about a better outcome.
“Well then, let me ask. What kind of position does that Zou hold in this household?”

To be honest, it reminds me of a certain pig I encountered back when I was in Japan. She’s either the daughter of a well-to-do family or is looked down upon by her own family. After all, she’s an elephant in the mammoth clan. You can tell at a glance that there’s probably some reason behind it.

“Lord Elmero… within the Puhant family… despite being born to the same parents, was born as a member of a different race… I understand the cause lies with a family member from several generations ago.”

That’s what the rat beastman said. Apparently, within the Mammoth clan, the elephant was born as an elephant due to recessive inheritance. Because of this, he was the subject of ridicule within the clan, and it was apparently decided from the very beginning that he would not be permitted to inherit the family line.

Attitudes toward this vary widely even among the races of Siltvelt, but apparently, the family line isn’t passed down through a single heir. He was explaining some rather confusing rules… but it seems to be something akin to a surname.

It’s a surname, yet not quite a surname; he isn’t allowed to inherit the family line, but he can speak of his surname. It’s a rather baffling concept. It’s a bit like being a knight but not a noble, I suppose? In any case, it seems Zou was born with a predetermined place within the family.
And, partly because of his appearance—which didn’t resemble his parents’—he was raised as the lowest-ranking member of the clan, mistreated and deprived of parental affection.
“Upon witnessing such unfortunate circumstances, Lady Rainy-Janon took Lord Elmero in, effectively taking him into her care from the Puhant family.”
“Who is that?”
“He is a noble whom we, along with some other servants of the Puhant family, used to serve.”
At this point, the rat beastman took out a small image crystal and showed it to me. It was the elderly rat from the painting Zou had been looking at.
“I see… So he’s Zou’s foster father, then.”

“Yes. Lady Rainy was renowned in Siltvelt as a brilliant strategist, so given the debt of gratitude we owed her, her connections in talent development, and her influence, the Puhant family could not refuse.”

The rat beastman went on to praise the elderly rat as if it were his own achievement. Apparently, there are various anecdotes about him—such as how, during a major battle in Siltvelt in the past, he saw through the strategies of the Wise King and worked tirelessly to minimize casualties. It’s said that if it weren’t for this elderly mouse, it wouldn’t be surprising if Siltvelt had been driven into an even worse situation. As for factions, it seems he belonged to the Genmu faction. The elders do seem to get along quite well.

“Lord Elmero was taken in under the pretext of assisting Lord Rainy, and under the guise of ‘chores,’ he was taught a wide range of things—from general education to martial arts. I still remember the events of that time… It was a very leisurely and peaceful time.”

I could sort of tell that the lives of Zou, the elderly mouse, and the servant mice were peaceful. The story unfolds about the life shared between the young Zou—who had been raised in contempt since before he could even understand right from wrong—and the small, elderly mouse.

At first, the elephant seemed frightened, but thanks to the elderly mouse’s devoted encouragement, he gradually opened up—such were their days at the elderly mouse’s mansion. The elderly mouse took on the role of teacher, instructing the elephant in various things—apparently even teaching him martial arts. It’s truly a mystery how they managed the size difference. I suspect they must have used Magic or something of the sort.

Although he was a strategist, he was also said to have military achievements, so it’s quite possible he was quite capable in close combat as well. In this world, levels and ability scores—statistics—are what matter, so size isn’t everything. Even a mouse with high Attack Power could easily send an elephant flying. I’m sure that’s how he handled the elephant.

“After all, in his youth, Lord Rainy experienced a bloody feud within his own race and had no children of his own… so he doted on Lord Elmero as if he were his own son… Do you know what Lord Elmero excels at most?”
“Isn’t it fighting?”

According to Panda, he’s said to be one of the top five warriors even in Zeltoble. His movements were slow and heavy, but he seemed to have almost no openings. In fact, he even used that slowness as a decoy.
“Lord Elmero has a talent for music. Lady Rainy was particularly fond of his singing; she’d often request songs, and we’d even join in on the performance… We enjoyed it immensely as well.”

Come to think of it, Zou was practicing a chorus with Filolial-sama and the others. I suppose that was due to that influence. As for Zou’s singing… he certainly has a voice that carries very well. It was an operatic voice, you know. It seems he can sing other styles as well. The mouse servants all agree that Zou is a good singer.
“Why on earth was someone like Zou working as a mercenary?”

That old mouse himself is nowhere to be found. There are various possibilities—maybe they had a fight, or he was forcibly taken away—but based on my experience from my days as a pig, it’s probably that the old mouse died. The mouse Beastman’s expression darkened slightly as he answered my question.
“Well… it’s because Lady Rainy passed away at the end of her natural life, and with no heir to succeed her, the Janon family was disbanded.”
“Couldn’t Zou have taken over?”
I’m asking about a common outcome based on my experience dating pigs.

“As for Lord Elmero inheriting the Janon House, Lady Rainy undoubtedly foresaw that the Puhant House and various other houses would intervene… She must have been aware of the power dynamics after her own death as well… She did leave a will and such… but she couldn’t fully protect that member of the Genmu clan…”
“And so, the servants of the Janon family also ended up like this…” the rat-Beastman said in a tone of lament.

“When Lady Rainy was bedridden due to this matter, she said to Lord Elmero: ‘I’ll leave my knighthood in your care. If you don’t like it, leave that house… and go as you please, set out into the outside world. Nothing binds you. Please be happy, our songstress…” And so… Lady Elmero gave him a gentle push, and he accepted Lady Rainy’s words… After the funeral was over, he stayed at this mansion for a while before leaving the house.”

Hmm… Just looking at this background, it seems like a rather serious problem, much like those of the pigs. Well, the elephant’s situation is probably more serious than the pigs’. After all, the elephant is a good elephant. It would be rude to compare him to pigs. We’ve got to do something about this.
After all, Zou’s benefactor is also my benefactor. I must find a way to grant the Mouse Benefactor’s wish.

“Apparently, the reason he stayed at this house for a little while was to talk with the Puhant family about Lady Rainy, and to make sure her precious belongings wouldn’t be thrown away when she left the house…”
“It’s easy to imagine that the conversation didn’t go very well.”
“Yes…”

Given that family, it goes without saying that no matter how hard Zou tried, it would be like pushing against a door that won’t open or driving a nail into bran. It’s a waste of effort. It’s practically a given that they wouldn’t appreciate his efforts at all. That’s probably why he didn’t want to bring Father along.
“So, Zou’s status as a knight was bestowed upon him by that fellow, then?”
“Yes… that’s correct.”
From there, he drifted from place to place, becoming a rogue knight who worked as a mercenary in places like Zeltoble. I suppose that’s how he came to live as the Queen of the Earthquake.
“Why do you two serve this household?”
“To protect the place where Lord Elmero can return at any time… and also, thanks to a little bit of Lady Rainy’s influence still lingering, just enough to ensure we don’t lose our jobs.”
The rat-beastman gave a wry smile as he said this. Even I could tell that smile was filled with loneliness.

“I understand about Zou. So, what is this household plotting? Presumably, they’re trying to strip Zou of his position—after all his achievements—and marry off someone from a family they favor to Father… the Shield Hero, is that it?”
That much is easy to imagine just from their own conversations. It’s a messy family feud, isn’t it? It’s a problem that those snobby rich nobles used to get into all the time.
“Yes, that’s generally correct.”

Just as I thought. Based on my experience, I have a few solutions for this kind of situation… I hate to sound like one of those pigs, but there are various approaches I can take as a reference. What I often did was storm into the mansion with my companions and, riding the momentum, go to “pick her up”—shouting sentimental platitudes and emotional arguments to the snob, like, “I love you for who you are! I didn’t fall for you just because you’re rich! What’s so great about your family background anyway!” Then the pig would stop holing up and start doing all sorts of things—fighting the house or bolting out—and so on. It feels like it ends up solving everything, really.
“Spear Hero… please, help Lord Elmero.”
“Leave it to me.”
“He sounds like he’s going to say ‘I’ll slaughter them all’ again, doesn’t he?”

The slave points at me and says that. What’s that supposed to mean? It’s as if I’m the kind of guy who can only kill people. That said, it’d be nice to slaughter those mammoths who’ve been causing trouble for Father and Zou.
“If that’s what you want, it’d be easy enough to wipe them out without leaving a single corpse behind. That’d keep the peace for a while.”

It’d also be easy if the entire clan suddenly went missing. In my current situation, I could gather intel, infiltrate meetings where problematic factions are gathering, and use something like the Liberation Firefloor to wipe out entire rooms—leaving no bodies behind—making it easy to eliminate troublemakers. As for the evil factions exploiting Father, the only solution is to eliminate them.

Come to think of it, when I first started the loop and arrived in Siltvelt, I probably should have looked for anyone holding a suspicious meeting and taken them out. Siltvelt isn’t exactly united, after all. Eliminating them secretly without leaving any evidence might be an effective strategy. After all, someone from the Mammoth clan might have been mixed in among those at the meeting. It might have killed two birds with one stone.
“Hey, hey, are you really sure this is okay!?”
“Hmm…”
Well, I suppose I can resolve this without going that far.
“It’ll be fine! Zou will definitely tear this house to shreds!”

There’s not much for me to do, really. Or maybe I should storm into Zou’s place and spout some passionate, high-sounding nonsense like I did to the pig? Zou is a great guy, and I do like him, but could I really express my affection with the same passion as I did back then?

……I don’t think so. Now that I’ve awakened to true love, Filo-tan is number one for me. I think I could say the same thing to Father, but what’s the point of trying to win Zou over? This might actually be a job best left to Father. Or maybe I should leave it to Kou.
I’ll have to ask Kou about this properly. Do I love Zou as a member of the opposite sex—enough to love her for the rest of my life?

I have a hunch that Kou’s feelings for Zou are about the same as those of Big Sister and her friends. I remember that his attitude toward her isn’t the same as it was when he was close to the wife he created based on Big Sister. But who knows when that might change. Let’s try asking Kou about it in a roundabout way.
……I feel like I’m starting to understand how that guy felt when he introduced me to that pig back in middle school. He must have felt just like I do right now.

Of course, I’ll have to hear Father’s opinion as well. Judging by Zou’s attitude, Father’s support might be more effective. The time has come for me to pass on to Father some spirited encouragement based on my own “pig” experiences.
“Hey, there’s this guy named Elmero who’s been whispered to by that guy and looks like he’s about to go on a rampage…”
“I-I hope he’ll be all right… And please stop insulting Elmero-sama.”
“Thanks for the info. Well then, I’ll be off!”
I’ve gathered all the intel I need. I’ll briefly go into stealth mode and resume my movement.
“H-he’s gone!”
“I haven’t gone anywhere. I heard what I needed to hear, so I’m just heading back.”
“A-all I can hear is his voice… What a terrifying technique…”
And so, having concluded my exchange with the rat Beastmen and their slaves, I returned to the room where Kou and the others were holding down the fort.
